The test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` is failing because the `FastDateFormat` class's formatting of the "z" timezone pattern does not respect the timezone of the `Calendar` instance passed to its format method.

The test tries to format a `Calendar` instance with a non-default timezone using `FastDateFormat`. It compares the output with the output of a `SimpleDateFormat` configured with the same pattern and timezone. The outputs differ because `FastDateFormat` always prints the default machine timezone's name for the "z" pattern, ignoring the timezone set on the `Calendar`, even though it prints the time correctly adjusted to the calendar's timezone.

The `FastDateFormat.format(Calendar)` method delegates to a `printer` object's `format(Calendar)` method (line 420). However, the underlying problem is that the timezone associated with the calendar is not used when formatting the timezone abbreviation or name ("z") in the pattern.

The issue arises because `FastDateFormat` internally likely uses a cached timezone (e.g., default time zone of the JVM or the one it was constructed with) or its own timezone management rather than dynamically reading the timezone from the passed `Calendar`. This results in printing the default timezone name instead of the actual calendar's timezone name.

The recent bug reports retrieved do not appear relevant to this timezone formatting issue.

Summary of diagnosis:
- The FastDateFormat.format(Calendar) delegates formatting to a printer.
- The printer does not correctly use the Calendar's timezone when formatting timezone pattern letters.
- As a result, the "z" timezone pattern always uses the JVM default timezone instead of the Calendar's timezone.
- This causes the observed test failure where the expected and actual timezone abbreviations do not match.

This matches the issue report complaint that the timezone pattern "z" is always rendered as the machine's default timezone ignoring the calendar's timezone.

The root cause is a design/implementation deficiency in FastDateFormat related to timezone handling when formatting Calendar instances with timezone patterns.

Next, it would be useful to see the code of the printer's format(Calendar) method or relevant timezone formatting internals to confirm the exact mechanics and locate where the calendar timezone is ignored.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
